subject.title: feat(browser): send pages to OpenClaw from the Chrome extension

question: Should OpenClaw accept bundled Chrome page sharing with a new public `system-event-runtime` resolver and additional extension permissions after the mechanical safety fixes land?
rationale: The patch is not only a bug repair: it adds a user-facing browser-ingress mode, broadens extension capabilities, and expands the plugin SDK contract, so maintainers must choose the permanent product and ownership boundary.

options.title: Sponsor bounded browser sharing
options.body: Keep the feature in the bundled browser plugin after fixing the lazy lifecycle, selection privacy, Google Docs routing, and connection-correlated acknowledgement defects.

options.title: Defer the new ingress surface
options.body: Pause the PR and revisit the page-sharing/SDK contract through a narrower maintainer-led design before adding browser permissions and public SDK exports.

recommendation.title: Sponsor bounded browser sharing
recommendation.body: Keep the feature in the bundled browser plugin after fixing the lazy lifecycle, selection privacy, Google Docs routing, and connection-correlated acknowledgement defects.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied history shows direct ownership of the proposed browser, relay, and SDK implementation, making this the best available routing candidate.
